lesson.subject: science

misconceptionProbe.signal: Ava thinks all liquids are water.
misconceptionProbe.checkPrompt: Is honey a liquid even though it moves slowly?
misconceptionProbe.expectedConfusion: Thinking thickness means it is not a liquid.

blocks.title: Chef Ava's Kitchen
blocks.prompt: Welcome! Today we use science to cook. Let's explore solids, liquids, and gases in your kitchen.

blocks.title: Matter Matters
blocks.prompt: Solids keep their shape. Liquids flow and take the shape of their container. Gases fill the whole space.

blocks.title: Kitchen Sort
blocks.prompt: Sort these kitchen items into the right group: Apple, Milk, Steam.

blocks.title: Quick Check
blocks.prompt: What state of matter is the orange juice in your glass?

blocks.title: Learning Recap
blocks.prompt: Ava learned to identify solids, liquids, and gases using cooking examples.

sceneSpec.title: Alchemist's Pot
sceneSpec.instruction: Move the heat slider and watch ice, water, and steam appear.
sceneSpec.helperText: Watch what happens when the heat gets higher and higher.
sceneSpec.rewardFact: Heat changes how fast tiny pieces move inside matter.

stages.label: liquid
stages.fact: A liquid can flow and pour.

stages.label: gas
stages.fact: A gas spreads into the air.

hintLadder.text: Think about if the item can pour or if it stays still.
If you put it in a bowl, does it change its shape?
A spoon is a solid. Is the soup more like a spoon or water?

lesson.parentSummary: Ava explored the three states of matter by categorizing common kitchen items like milk, fruit, and steam.
